stage: built and rendered; desktop 1440x1000 and phone 390x844 exercised with a real click on 2026-10-04

choice-justified:grouped-tile-map.why: The question is which family each project belongs to and what a visitor can open, across 25 projects at once. One tile per project inside four enclosed family groups puts membership, today's format and interface state on one screen, so a misplaced project or a weak family shows as a tile in the wrong box. This is the router's small-multiples idea applied to one frame per family.

rejected:project-schedule.why: Router's top score, but nothing here has dates or durations; a schedule would invent a time axis.

rejected:timeline.why: No time dimension in the question.

rejected:requirements-traceability-matri.why: A project-by-attribute matrix shows the same facts but hides the grouping, which is the thing being decided.

rejected:three-full-page-mockups.why: Drawing today, one format and two formats each with 25 labelled marks would be about 78 objects against a 40-object budget; today's layout is aggregated into three bars instead.

title-states-what-this-is-and-for-whom.why: The h1 is the one question; the line under it says it is for Brian, a proposal, dated, nothing built.

whole-design-visible-on-one-screen-at-th.why: The 1440x1000 capture shows title through detail panel with no scrolling. After a project is selected the detail panel grows by a few lines and the page becomes slightly taller than the viewport; the panel stays visible because it sticks to the bottom.

cold-reader-gets-the-mechanism-in-sixty-.why: No cold reader has read it. Brian is the first reader.

form-matches-job-lists-scan-tables-compa.why: Grouping is shown as enclosed groups, counts as bars, format options as small mock layouts, the three calls as short text.

relationships-drawn-not-implied-by-adjac.why: Family membership is a drawn enclosure; interface state is fill, border style and glyph; today's format and the shown-twice cases are a written tag on each tile.

same-object-same-mark-across-every-view.why: Each project appears once, as one tile. The side mock-ups do not redraw projects.

every-object-reveals-more-on-click-nothi.why: All 25 project tiles open a detail panel (checked with a real click at 1440 and 390 wide). Family headings and the three side boxes are not clickable.

one-primary-drawing-with-callouts-not-pa.why: The family map takes most of the screen. The decision box above it is three short text calls, kept as text because they are choices, not structure.

attributed-claims-traced-to-source-no-in.why: Every tile is generated from an inventory parsed from the page source at portfolio main f6dafa1; counts are asserted in the generator (25 projects; 16, 8 and 1 by state; 5, 8, 7 and 5 by family). Short names and family assignments are the agent's and are labelled draft on the page.

structural-devices-encode-information-no.why: Fill and border style mean interface state, enclosure means family. The only decoration is rounded corners and a shadow on the detail panel.

no-generated-defaults-cream-serif-card-k.why: System sans font, no cream, no all-caps labels (removed after first render), no middle dots. The regions are plain bordered boxes, which is close to a card kit; kept because the boxes are the groups.

each-concept-drawn-in-a-shape-that-mirro.why: One format is drawn as identical bars, two formats as bars plus thin dashed rows, three formats as three bars of different length.

white-space-separates-groups-and-carries.why: 14px between families, 5px between tiles inside one.

size-and-weight-follow-importance.why: Title largest, decision box has the heaviest border, project names bold, tags and status small and grey.

structure-earned-by-content-not-imposed-.why: The page's own structure is decision, map, legend. The four families are the proposal under review, not a settled taxonomy, and the three borderline projects are marked.

page-carries-its-date-and-version.why: Date in the opening line; source commits in the status line; the plans site labels the page with its own commit.

each-element-encodes-its-answer-visually.why: The decision box is text. It was not redrawn as a picture.

each-drawing-shows-relations-a-list-cann.why: Family sizes, the mix of usable and recording-only projects in each family, and the lone project with nothing to open are visible at once; a list would lose the comparison between families.

one-element-dominates-by-size-weight-or-.why: The family map dominates by area and colour. The decision box competes by border weight, deliberately, because it is what Brian must answer.

reading-order-is-obvious-without-instruc.why: Top to bottom: title, decision, map, legend, status, detail.

enclosure-nesting-at-most-two-levels.why: Family box then tile; decision box then call.

elements-share-a-small-set-of-edges.why: One sidebar edge and four column edges on a grid.

same-role-same-treatment-everywhere.why: All tiles share one structure; all side boxes share one.

every-mark-carries-information.why: Glyph and fill both mean interface state (doubled on purpose so it reads without colour), the tag means today's format, the question mark means borderline.

context-quiet-subject-loud.why: Side boxes and status are grey; project tiles carry the colour.

comparisons-use-identical-small-frames.why: The one-format and two-format mock-ups use the same frame. Today's formats are bars of counts, a different form because it is a count, not a layout.

every-encoding-explained-on-the-same-scr.why: The legend sits under the map inside the 1440x1000 screen.

one-highlighted-state-not-several.why: Only the selected project gets the dark outline.

object-count-within-density-budget-or-ag.why: 25 tiles, 4 family boxes, 3 side boxes and 1 decision box is 33 objects against a budget of 40; today's 28 entries are aggregated into three bars.

headline-and-picture-alone-convey-the-po.why: The headline asks the question and the picture shows four families of same-shaped tiles.

no-block-of-prose-longer-than-the-drawin.why: The longest text is the decision box, about 130 words, above a map of 25 tiles.

reader-can-point-to-where-any-one-fact-l.why: Counts live in the Today box, interface state in the tile fill, links in the detail panel, sources in the status line.

wrong-if: Brian asks which projects to drop or feature rather than how to group them (then the job was ranking, and a ranked list was the form)
Brian cannot tell usable from recording-only tiles without colour
the 390px render needs horizontal scroll (checked: it does not)
a project's family is disputed for more than the three marked borderline
router-gaps: primary scored project-schedule again on a question with no time axis
no catalog entry for a grouped tile map (hierarchy by enclosure with a state badge); small-multiples was the nearest
not-verified: how the sticky detail panel behaves on a real phone (the phone layout instead places the panel under the tapped tile; checked in a 390x844 headless browser only)
whether each project link gives a visitor a result in one click

choice-justified:project-schedule.why: Not chosen. The router's top score was a schedule, but nothing in this question has dates or durations. The page is a grouped tile map instead; the reasoning is under choice-justified:grouped-tile-map.
